correctness.rationale: Exact normalized beta moments and two Stieltjes primitives reconstruct the affine derivative of each projected jump. Integrating its absolute value gives a complete two-branch step variation function; differentiating yields the verified quadratic Q_c, with one off-centre positive maximum candidate. A strict logarithmic inequality proves the off-centre candidate dominates the central one for every c>3. Signed-measure decomposition of BV inputs and triangle inequality give the universal upper bound; one jump attains equality and opposite-sign affine profiles exclude two-site mixtures. Root and beta limits follow analytically. The standalone Python checker passed exact rational moment tests, independent affine derivative integration, randomized signed-jump inequality, and parameter asymptotic diagnostics; finite tests were not treated as proof.

value.rationale: Unweighted total variation provides a natural stability measurement for discontinuous input signals under an exact polynomial projector and differs fundamentally from prior pointwise range/Gibbs quantities. This result determines all shape parameters, a sharp root-based norm, complete extremizer geometry and two asymptotic boundary regimes, revealing unavoidable off-centre jump instability and linear-in-weight growth. It is a parameter-uniform structural classification rather than a small fixed-case computation.
